newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may price next Svyazinvest stake higher.
newsitem.headline: Russia may price next Svyazinvest stake higher.

text.p: The longer Russia takes to sell off a second, 24 percent stake in telecommunications holding giant Svyazinvest, the higher the price will be, a top government official said on Friday.
Results for the first sale, at which 25 percent plus one share are being auctioned at a starting price of $1.18 billion, are due to be announced after 5 p.m. (1300 GMT).
"The terms of the 24 percent sale depend on the time frame," Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Bulgak told Ekho-Moskvy radio.
"If the property fund decides it is necessary to sell this year, the starting price will practically be the same (as the $1.18 billion price tag for the first auction).
"If it is done in a year or two, the starting price may rise, since the price of its shares is rising."
Earlier this week, Svyazinvest chief executive officer Nail Ismailov said the second, 24 percent stake, which will be sold only to Russian investors, would be auctioned in about six months.
Svyazinvest holds controlling stakes in 88 regional telecoms, including the Rostelekom RTKM.RTS long-distance carrier.
The Svyazinvest sale, Russia's largest privatisation to date, is being closely watched for signs of transparency in Moscow's sell-off of state property.
Telecoms shares have long been hottest stocks on the Russian share market, which has risen by about 30 percent last month.
